title: Sixth Word Five Degrees Of Profit From Selling The Trust

questions.question: What is the first benefit of giving one’s temporary life and possessions for Allah’s sake?
questions.answer: What is temporary is turned into something lasting, and a passing life brings eternal results.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the final outcome of moments that seem to disappear in this world?
questions.answer: They do not end in useless loss; they become enduring blessings in the life to come.

questions.question: Besides eternal life, what other state is mentioned for the fruits of a faithful life before the final resurrection?
questions.answer: They also appear in a bright and comforting way in the intermediate state after death.

questions.question: What is the second benefit named in the passage?
questions.answer: Paradise is given as the return.

questions.question: What general change happens to the human faculties when they are used for Allah?
questions.answer: Their worth rises greatly.

questions.question: What example is used first to explain the third benefit?
questions.answer: The intellect.

questions.question: What happens to the intellect if a person uses it only for the lower self?
questions.answer: It becomes harmful and wears the person down with grief about the past and fear of the future.

questions.question: According to the passage, why do some sinful people run toward intoxication or empty entertainment?
questions.answer: They try to escape the distress caused by a misused intellect.

questions.question: What does the intellect become when it is used on behalf of its true Owner?
questions.answer: It becomes a means of opening deep truths, mercy, and wisdom.

questions.question: What higher role does the intellect then take on for the person?
questions.answer: It guides the person toward everlasting happiness.

questions.question: What is the eye called in relation to the spirit?
questions.answer: It is presented as an opening through which the spirit observes the world.

questions.question: What happens to the eye when it is used only to chase temporary beauty and desire?
questions.answer: It falls into serving lust.

questions.question: What happens to the eye when it is used within the boundaries set by Allah?
questions.answer: It becomes a way of reading creation and seeing signs of divine artistry and mercy.

questions.question: What faculty is discussed after the eye?
questions.answer: The tongue together with the sense of taste.

questions.question: What happens to taste when it is used only for appetite and the lower self?
questions.answer: It sinks into a low service role centered only on the stomach.

questions.question: What happens to taste when it is used for the sake of the Generous Provider?
questions.answer: It rises to a noble role of recognizing and appreciating divine provision.

questions.question: What does the passage ask the reader to do with the other limbs and faculties?
questions.answer: Compare them by the same pattern as the examples already given.

questions.question: What kind of character does a believer develop by using the trust properly?
questions.answer: A character suited for Paradise.

questions.question: What kind of character does an unbeliever develop by misusing the trust?
questions.answer: A character suited for Hell.

questions.question: What is the reason given for the difference between the believer and the unbeliever in this matter?
questions.answer: The believer uses what was entrusted by the Creator in the Creator’s way and limits, while the unbeliever uses it for the lower self.

questions.question: What human condition is emphasized at the start of the fourth benefit?
questions.answer: Human beings are helpless, needy, weak, and surrounded by many hardships.

questions.question: What happens to a person who does not rely on Allah, trust Him, and submit to Him?
questions.answer: The person’s inner life becomes disturbed and crushed by useless pain, regret, and distress.

questions.question: What extreme result can happen to a person under that inner pressure?
questions.answer: The person may become morally degraded, like a beast.

questions.question: Who are mentioned as confirming the fifth benefit?
questions.answer: People of spiritual insight and those who have witnessed deeper realities.

questions.question: What do these spiritually aware people agree about?
questions.answer: They agree that worship and remembrance done through one’s bodily faculties will return as rewards from Paradise when one needs them most.

questions.question: At what time will those rewards be especially given?
questions.answer: At the moment of greatest need.

questions.question: Into what does temporary property change in the first benefit?
questions.answer: It becomes everlasting.

questions.question: What condition is attached to this transformation of life into something eternal?
questions.answer: Life must be devoted to Allah and used for His sake.

questions.question: How does the passage portray the moments of life at first glance?
questions.answer: They seem to fade away and decay.

questions.question: What do those same moments become in the eternal realm?
questions.answer: They become flourishing blessings and good outcomes.

questions.question: What added comfort is mentioned concerning those deeds before the final hereafter?
questions.answer: They also show a radiant and reassuring side in the intermediate world after death.

questions.question: What is received as the exchange in the second benefit?
questions.answer: Paradise.

questions.question: What broad claim is made at the start of the third benefit about body parts and senses?
questions.answer: Every limb and faculty gains far greater value.

questions.question: If the mind is used for selfish desire, what two time-related burdens does it place on a person?
questions.answer: It loads the person with sorrow tied to the past and fear tied to the future.

questions.question: In that corrupted state, what kind of instrument does the mind become?
questions.answer: A damaging and troublesome one.

questions.question: When the mind is used for Allah, what does it unlock?
questions.answer: Deep stores of mercy and wisdom found in creation.

questions.question: How does that proper use of the mind affect the owner’s future?
questions.answer: It prepares the owner for eternal happiness.

questions.question: What is wrong with using the eye only for passing attractions?
questions.answer: It lowers the eye into serving desire instead of truth.

questions.question: What honorable function does the eye gain when it is used properly?
questions.answer: It becomes a means of reading the world as a meaningful creation and witnessing divine signs.

questions.question: What image is used for the tongue and taste when they are misused?
questions.answer: They are reduced to low service for bodily appetite.

questions.question: What image is used for the tongue and taste when they are used rightly?
questions.answer: They become refined servants that recognize and appreciate Allah’s provision.

questions.question: Why does the passage give several examples from different faculties?
questions.answer: To show that the same principle applies to all human capacities.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does a believer gain through faithful use of the trust?
questions.answer: A nature fit for Paradise.

questions.question: What does an unbeliever gain through betrayal of the trust?
questions.answer: A nature fit for Hell.

questions.question: What is the key difference in how believer and unbeliever use that trust?
questions.answer: One uses it by Allah’s purpose and limits, while the other uses it for the lower self.

questions.question: What four human qualities are highlighted in the fourth benefit?
questions.answer: Helplessness, many troubles, poverty of means, and weakness.

questions.question: What is the proper response to those human limitations according to the passage?
questions.answer: Rely on Allah, trust Him, and submit to Him with confidence.

questions.question: What happens to the conscience when a person refuses that reliance?
questions.answer: It remains troubled.

questions.question: What kinds of inner suffering follow from that refusal?
questions.answer: Empty suffering, pain, and regret overwhelm the person.

questions.question: What group supports the claim in the fifth benefit?
questions.answer: Spiritually illuminated people and the elect who have seen the truth of things.

questions.question: What future reward do they testify to concerning worship done through one’s faculties?
questions.answer: It will return as fruits of Paradise at the time when one needs them most.

questions.question: What is the central idea of the first profit?
questions.answer: Giving what is temporary to Allah leads to permanence.

questions.question: Why does a life spent for Allah not count as wasted?
questions.answer: Because it produces everlasting benefit.

questions.question: How does the passage contrast outward appearance with deeper reality regarding life’s moments?
questions.answer: They seem to vanish, but in truth they continue as eternal blessings.

questions.question: In what two places are the results of such a life mentioned?
questions.answer: In the eternal realm and in the intermediate state after death.

questions.question: What is the second profit in one clear phrase?
questions.answer: Paradise is the payment.

questions.question: What does the third profit say happens to human powers and senses?
questions.answer: Their value is multiplied greatly.

questions.question: How is the intellect ruined when it serves the lower self?
questions.answer: It turns into a source of pain, weakness, and harmful anxiety.

questions.question: What emotional pattern does a corrupted intellect create?
questions.answer: It traps a person between sadness over what is gone and fear over what is coming.

questions.question: What behavior is said to follow from that torment in some sinful people?
questions.answer: They seek escape through intoxication or shallow amusement.

questions.question: When rightly used, what kind of instrument does the intellect become?
questions.answer: A key that opens understanding of divine mercy and wisdom.

questions.question: What does that tell us about knowledge in the passage?
questions.answer: True knowledge should lead a person toward Allah and eternal joy.

questions.question: How is the eye degraded when used for the self alone?
questions.answer: It becomes a servant of desire focused on fleeting attractions.

questions.question: How is the eye elevated when used for Allah?
questions.answer: It becomes a viewer of the signs of creation and mercy.

questions.question: What is the negative result of using the tongue and taste only for the stomach?
questions.answer: They are lowered to a crude bodily function without higher meaning.

questions.question: What is the positive result of using the tongue and taste for Allah?
questions.answer: They become means of grateful awareness of divine generosity.

questions.question: Why does the passage call the reader to compare all the other limbs with these examples?
questions.answer: To help the reader apply the lesson across the whole person.

questions.question: What connection does the passage make between belief and one’s inner nature?
questions.answer: Belief shapes a person into someone suited for Paradise.

questions.question: What connection does the passage make between disbelief and one’s inner nature?
questions.answer: Disbelief shapes a person into someone suited for Hell.

questions.question: What moral principle explains this difference?
questions.answer: Whether the person is faithful or treacherous with the Creator’s trust.

questions.question: According to the fourth profit, what is human life like without dependence on Allah?
questions.answer: It becomes crushing because people are weak and needy but try to carry life alone.

questions.question: What three attitudes toward Allah are urged in the fourth profit?
questions.answer: Reliance, trust, and willing submission.

questions.question: What happens inside a person who refuses those attitudes?
questions.answer: The conscience is disturbed and burdened.

questions.question: What figurative outcome describes the person’s moral decline in that state?
questions.answer: The person is reduced to an animal-like condition.

questions.question: Who agrees on the truth of the fifth profit?
questions.answer: Those with spiritual illumination and deep witnessing of reality.

questions.question: What exactly will be returned to the believer according to the fifth profit?
questions.answer: The reward of worship and glorification done through the body and faculties.

questions.question: Why is the timing of that return important?
questions.answer: It comes when the person needs it most.

questions.question: What change happens to passing possessions in the first profit?
questions.answer: They are made enduring.

questions.question: What must a person do for this change to happen to his life?
questions.answer: He must dedicate it to Allah and spend it for His sake.

questions.question: What image is used for life’s moments before their deeper value appears?
questions.answer: They are like things that seem to wither away.

questions.question: What do those moments produce beyond this world?
questions.answer: They produce lasting blessings and good fruits.

questions.question: What comforting truth is given about the state after death?
questions.answer: Those deeds also appear there in a bright and hopeful form.

questions.question: What is the reward named in the second profit?
questions.answer: Paradise.

questions.question: What is the main teaching of the third profit in general?
questions.answer: Human faculties become far more valuable when used for Allah.

questions.question: How does misuse of the intellect affect a person’s emotional life?
questions.answer: It fills the person with distress from memory and fear.

questions.question: What does that misuse show about intellect by itself?
questions.answer: It is not enough on its own; its direction matters.

questions.question: How does the rightly guided intellect function?
questions.answer: It opens up the meanings, wisdom, and mercy within creation.

questions.question: What final benefit does the rightly guided intellect bring?
questions.answer: It helps lead its owner to eternal happiness.

questions.question: What lowers the eye according to the passage?
questions.answer: Using it to pursue temporary attractions for selfish desire.

questions.question: What raises the eye according to the passage?
questions.answer: Using it under Allah’s guidance to observe the signs in creation.

questions.question: What is the low use of the tongue and taste?
questions.answer: Serving appetite alone.

questions.question: What is the high use of the tongue and taste?
questions.answer: Recognizing divine generosity with gratitude.

questions.question: What conclusion should the reader draw about all the other limbs?
questions.answer: They too can either sink through misuse or rise through proper use.

questions.question: What kind of person does faithful use of one’s faculties help form?
questions.answer: A person fit for Paradise.

questions.question: What kind of person does selfish misuse of one’s faculties help form?
questions.answer: A person fit for Hell.

questions.question: What is the believer doing with the Creator’s trust?
questions.answer: Using it as it was meant to be used and staying within the limits set by Allah.

questions.question: What is the unbeliever doing with that same trust?
questions.answer: Betraying it by using it for the lower self.

questions.question: In the fourth profit, what is one reason human beings need divine reliance?
questions.answer: They face many disasters and needs while being weak and helpless.

questions.question: What is the effect on the conscience if a person will not trust Allah?
questions.answer: It becomes restless and troubled.

questions.question: What can those inner pains do to a person?
questions.answer: They can overwhelm him and lower him morally.

questions.question: Who are cited as witnesses for the fifth profit?
questions.answer: Spiritually awakened people and those granted direct insight into reality.

questions.question: What do these witnesses say about acts of worship done through the body?
questions.answer: Their reward will be given back as fruits of Paradise.

questions.question: When will those fruits matter most?
questions.answer: At the time of greatest need.

questions.question: According to the first profit, what happens to a fading worldly life when it is offered to Allah?
questions.answer: It becomes connected to eternity and yields lasting results.

questions.question: Why are the moments of a righteous life not truly lost?
questions.answer: Because they grow into enduring blessings beyond this world.

questions.question: What two realms are mentioned for the appearance of these results?
questions.answer: The eternal world and the intermediate realm after death.

questions.question: What is the second profit stated very simply?
questions.answer: The return is Paradise.

questions.question: What is the core message of the third profit?
questions.answer: Every human faculty becomes much more valuable when used for Allah.

questions.question: What is the negative example given for the intellect?
questions.answer: If it serves the lower self, it harms the person instead of helping him.

questions.question: What kinds of thoughts make that misused intellect painful?
questions.answer: Sorrows about what is past and fears about what is ahead.

questions.question: What coping habits are mentioned as signs of this misuse?
questions.answer: Drunkenness and pointless entertainment.

questions.question: What is the positive example given for the intellect?
questions.answer: It becomes a means of opening the hidden mercy and wisdom in creation.

questions.question: What does that say about the best use of human reasoning?
questions.answer: It should lead to truth, guidance, and eternal success.

questions.question: What is the eye meant to become when used rightly?
questions.answer: A perceiver of the meanings and signs placed in the world by Allah.

questions.question: What does the eye become when used wrongly?
questions.answer: A servant of lust focused on temporary beauty.

questions.question: What is the low state of the tongue and taste when they are misdirected?
questions.answer: They are reduced to serving appetite only.

questions.question: What is their high state when they are directed to Allah?
questions.answer: They become grateful recognizers of divine provision.

questions.question: Why does the passage call attention to the contrast between low and high uses of the faculties?
questions.answer: To show how belief transforms ordinary human powers into noble ones.

questions.question: What does the believer gain in terms of inner character?
questions.answer: A nature that belongs with Paradise.

questions.question: What does the unbeliever gain in terms of inner character?
questions.answer: A nature that belongs with Hell.

questions.question: What practical difference causes these opposite outcomes?
questions.answer: The believer uses Allah’s trust as commanded, while the unbeliever uses it for selfish impulses.

questions.question: What does the fourth profit teach about human independence?
questions.answer: Human beings cannot carry life well by themselves because they are weak and needy.

questions.question: What three spiritual acts are presented as the right response?
questions.answer: Depending on Allah, trusting Him, and submitting to Him.

questions.question: What happens if a person refuses that response?
questions.answer: The person is choked by useless suffering, pain, and regret.

questions.question: How severe can the moral damage become?
questions.answer: The person may sink into a beast-like condition.

questions.question: In the fifth profit, who confirms the truth of the promised reward?
questions.answer: People with spiritual unveiling and insight into reality.

questions.question: What kinds of actions are included in the reward mentioned there?
questions.answer: Acts of worship and glorification performed through the body and its faculties.

questions.question: In what form will that reward be granted?
questions.answer: As fruits of Paradise.

questions.question: Why is that future reward especially meaningful?
questions.answer: It comes at the moment when the person most needs help.

questions.question: What basic transformation is described in the first profit?
questions.answer: Something temporary is turned into something everlasting.

questions.question: What must happen for one’s life to gain eternal fruit?
questions.answer: It must be given to Allah and spent in His cause.

questions.question: How does the passage correct the idea that life’s moments simply disappear?
questions.answer: It says they continue as blessed results in the eternal world.

questions.question: What additional place is mentioned where these results appear with comfort and light?
questions.answer: The intermediate realm after death.

questions.question: What is offered in exchange in the second profit?
questions.answer: Paradise.

questions.question: What broad principle does the third profit teach about human abilities?
questions.answer: Their value rises immensely when they are used as Allah intended.

questions.question: What does the intellect become when it is ruled by the lower self?
questions.answer: A harmful burden that increases sorrow and fear.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest this wrong use of intellect can drive a sinner toward?
questions.answer: Escapes such as intoxication or shallow pleasures.

questions.question: What does the intellect become when returned to its true purpose?
questions.answer: A key that opens understanding of divine mercy and wisdom.

questions.question: What future-oriented role does the rightly used intellect play?
questions.answer: It prepares a person for eternal happiness.

questions.question: What is the eye’s proper dignity in the passage?
questions.answer: It is a means of seeing the signs and artistry of Allah in creation.

questions.question: What degrades the eye from that dignity?
questions.answer: Using it for selfish desire and chasing passing beauty.

questions.question: What lowers the tongue and taste from their proper rank?
questions.answer: Using them only for bodily appetite and the lower self.

questions.question: What raises the tongue and taste to a noble rank?
questions.answer: Using them with gratitude toward the One who provides sustenance.

questions.question: What is the reader expected to infer about the rest of the human faculties?
questions.answer: They follow the same rule of either rising through faithful use or falling through selfish use.

questions.question: What kind of existential outcome does the believer develop through proper use of the trust?
questions.answer: A being and character suitable for Paradise.

questions.question: What kind of existential outcome does the unbeliever develop through misuse?
questions.answer: A being and character suitable for Hell.

questions.question: What is the direct cause of this difference according to the passage?
questions.answer: One is faithful to the Creator’s trust and the other betrays it for the lower self.

questions.question: What truths about human life are emphasized in the fourth profit?
questions.answer: People are weak, needy, vulnerable, and surrounded by troubles.

questions.question: What inner effect follows when a person does not lean on Allah?
questions.answer: The conscience remains in turmoil.

questions.question: What kinds of suffering then take over the person?
questions.answer: Pointless torment, pain, and regret.

questions.question: What final degrading result may follow?
questions.answer: The person may lose human nobility and become beast-like.

questions.question: What kind of people affirm the fifth profit?
questions.answer: Those granted spiritual illumination and direct insight into truth.

questions.question: What do they affirm about the worship done through human limbs and faculties?
questions.answer: It will be rewarded in the form of the blessings of Paradise.

questions.question: When will that reward be delivered?
questions.answer: At the time of greatest need.

questions.question: Looking across all five profits, what is the overall message of the passage?
questions.answer: Surrendering one’s faculties and life to Allah does not diminish a person; it elevates, secures, and eternally rewards the person.
